By contrast, the SM-102-based reference LNP tested under the same conditions showed aggregation and reduced reporter expression after nebulization. Non-nebulized mucLP3 also supported mRNA expression in airway epithelial cell lines, mouse lung organoids, and primary human airway epithelial cultures maintained at an air-liquid interface. These data establish a proof of concept for a PEG-free lipid-polymer hybrid architecture that tolerates the tested nebulization procedure and remains functional in respiratory models of increasing complexity. Direct mucus-transport measurements, aerosol-deposition studies, and in vivo efficacy studies will be required to establish pulmonary delivery performance.

articles.title: Bola-amphiphilic dendrimers with tunable architecture for ROS-responsive precision delivery of doxorubicin.
articles.abstract: Stimuli-responsive nanocarriers capable of precise intracellular drug release are critical for improving the efficacy and safety of cancer chemotherapy. However, many existing systems suffer from limited structural tunability and incomplete integration of molecular architecture, self-assembly, and responsiveness, which constrains tumor delivery and therapeutic performance. Here, we report reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive bola-amphiphilic dendrimers with tunable dendron generations, bola4A and bola8A, as a platform for doxorubicin (DOX) delivery and systematic comparison. Both dendrimers displayed high drug-loading capacities and stable nanoassembly formation, whereas bola4A, with lower-generation PAMAM dendrons, permitted more efficient stimulus penetration into the nanosystems. This architectural feature enhanced ROS- and pH-triggered drug release, promoted cellular uptake, and accelerated endosomal escape. Importantly, modulation of dendron generation systematically altered nanoparticle architecture and responsiveness, directly dictating therapeutic efficacy. Consequently, bola4A/DOX nanoparticles achieved superior tumor accumulation and tissue penetration, together with improved anticancer efficacy in vitro and in ovarian cancer SKOV3 xenograft models and reduced systemic toxicity relative to free DOX. These results establish dendritic architecture as a key determinant of stimuli-responsiveness and drug delivery performance, and provide a rational framework for the design of next-generation stimuli-responsive nanomedicines tailored to pathological microenvironments.

articles.title: Probiotic-loaded biomaterial for wound healing and tissue regeneration: a unique medical tool.
articles.abstract: Deeper skin wounds lead to infections prolonging the healing process resulting in further complications. Although the treatment protocol includes mostly the use of antibiotics, the main challenge comes with their resistance and poor pharmacokinetics. Selective strain specific probiotic infused hydrogel system is one such newer approach in wound management to counter these issues. The highly sensitive probiotic strain needs proper conditions for colonization and protection against external environment. In this study, an economically feasible and simple attempt was made to incorporate the probiotics into a polymeric composite. Locust bean gum and gum odina were allowed to form a polymeric mix, into which Lactobacillus rhamnosus MTCC 5897, a probiotic was incorporated using CaCl2 as the crosslinker. The probiotic bound composite films were assessed for their microstructure, swelling ability, probiotic stability along with probiotic viability. Additionally, the antioxidant, cytocompatibility and antibacterial properties of the film were investigated. Furthermore, the in vivo wound model on rats indicated satisfactory healing rate along with collagen deposition. Therefore, the results demonstrated preliminary findings of the film that may act as a wound healing tool which further would require several clinical trials to be accepted commercially, and also paves way for further future research on advanced biomaterials focused on living bacterial hydrogel film providing wound healing potency.

articles.title: Impact of oxidative degradation on the bioavailability of subcutaneously administered adalimumab.
articles.abstract: Subcutaneous (SC) administration of therapeutic antibodies enhances patient convenience and healthcare resource efficiency compared to intravenous (IV) delivery, but therapy can be limited by incomplete bioavailability (BA) of SC biotherapeutics. This limitation may be attributed to processes inherent to the unique composition of SC tissue, including the potential presence of reactive oxygen species (ROS) within the SC microenvironment, which can induce chemical and structural instability and functional impairment. This study investigated the impact of oxidation on the SC BA of adalimumab (Humira® biosimilar) as a representative IgG1 therapeutic protein. Two models of oxidation, mimicking some of those ROS encountered in the SC tissue, were applied to adalimumab, then the resulting oxidized variants were characterized and subsequently administered SC to rats to evaluate changes in SC BA. HPLC-MS/MS analysis identified methionine residues within CH2-CH3 interface as the primary sites of oxidation. Oxidation at these sites correlated with reduced conformational stability, alterations in the charge variant profile, and diminished binding affinity to the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn). SC administration of oxidized species at 18% (w/w), diluted with excess unstressed IgG, to rats resulted in a slight decrease in SC BA, although not statistically significant. Additionally, oxidized AdmAb showed prolonged retention at the SC injection site, which may be associated with reduced conformational stability and higher propensity to aggregation and precipitation, although the underlaying mechanism requires further studies. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that oxidation can substantially alter the biophysical stability and FcRn binding affinity, while administering a moderate proportion of those oxidized species 18% (w/w) results in minimal changes in PK profile and overall SC BA.

articles.title: Peripheral GALR2 activation by the metabolically stabilized spexin analog LIT-01-144 produces potent opioid‑independent antinociception.
articles.abstract: Chronic pain constitutes a major global health burden, and current management remains largely dependent on opioid analgesics, which are associated with opioid use disorder. Accordingly, there is a pressing need to identify non-opioid therapeutic strategies. Galanin receptors (GALR1-3) have been implicated in pain modulation, but their individual roles remain insufficiently defined because of the absence of subtype-selective ligands. Recently, spexin has been identified as an endogenous peptide that selectively activates GALR2 and GALR3, offering a new scaffold for developing pharmacological tools targeting these receptor subtypes. In this study, we designed and characterized LIT-01-144, a modified spexin analog incorporating N-terminal fluorocarbon functionalization to improve metabolic stability while preserving receptor selectivity. In vitro pharmacological profiling demonstrated high potency at GALR2 and GALR3, with negligible activity at GALR1. Pharmacokinetic analyses showed a substantially prolonged plasma half-life relative to native spexin and no evidence of central nervous system penetration. In vivo, intracerebroventricular administration of LIT-01-144 produced robust antinociception at doses tenfold lower than those required for spexin. Although systemic administration had no detectable effect in naïve mice, it significantly attenuated pain-related behaviors in a model of persistent inflammatory pain. This effect was mediated specifically by GALR2 and was independent of opioid receptor signaling. In situ hybridization further showed an increase in Galr2 + neurons in dorsal root ganglia of inflamed mice. Collectively, these findings highlight GALR2 as a promising peripheral target for developing non-opioid analgesics and demonstrate the potential of LIT-01-144 as a valuable tool for understanding GALR2-mediated mechanisms of pain modulation.

articles.title: Adolescent-onset regular cannabis use is associated with altered neural and behavioural responses during anticipation and feedback of monetary reward and loss.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Regular cannabis use has been associated with alterations in reward-related neural processes, yet findings remain inconsistent and the relationship between neural activity and behavioural performance is not fully understood. OBJECTIVES: The present study aimed to characterise neural and behavioural correlates of reward processing in regular cannabis users (CU) compared with matched non-users (NU) using the Monetary Incentive Delay Task (MIDT). METHODS: Twenty adolescent-onset regular cannabis users (CU; ≥4 days/week for 2 years, with regular use initiated before age 18) and twenty age- and sex-matched non-users (NU) completed the Monetary Incentive Delay Task during functional MRI. Firstly, we assessed behavioural performance through reaction times, accuracy and monetary earnings to determine whether potential neural alterations were reflected in task performance. Secondly, focusing on reward-related brain regions, we examined group differences in BOLD functional MRI activity during anticipation and outcome phases separately for monetary win and loss conditions. Finally, we explored the association between behavioural performance and neural activation. RESULTS: Our findings provide preliminary evidence that adolescent-onset regular cannabis use is associated with altered engagement of key nodes within the mesocorticolimbic circuit accompanied by impaired behavioural performance. Particularly, compared with NU, CU showed (I) lower striatal activity during anticipation of monetary win and higher ventral striatum and frontal pole activity during anticipation of monetary loss; (II) different VTA BOLD contrast estimates during outcome of successful monetary win and loss avoidance, and lower frontal pole activity during outcome of unsuccessful loss avoidance; (III) lower monetary rewards and a trend towards slower reaction times and reduced accuracy; (IV) disrupted brain-behaviour coupling. CONCLUSIONS: Results from this study may help inform future research on the neurobiological mechanisms underlying changes in reward function and the resultant behavioural consequences of adolescent-onset cannabis use.

articles.title: Synthetic cannabinoid-induced changes in thalamo-prefrontal gamma synchrony and thalamic high-voltage spindles.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Cannabinoids, including Δ⁹-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and potent synthetic analogs, disrupt cognitive and perceptual processes via dysregulated neural oscillations. While these effects within limbic-cortical circuits have been well documented, the contribution of thalamocortical loops, which act as critical hubs for sensory gating and cognitive integration, remains unexplored. OBJECTIVES: To characterize the effects of acute synthetic cannabinoid exposure on thalamo-prefrontal oscillatory dynamics, specifically focusing on local gamma power, inter-regional synchrony, and cross-frequency coupling relevant. METHODS: We performed simultaneous local field potential (LFP) recordings from the mediodorsal thalamus (MD), prelimbic (PrL), and orbitofrontal (OFC) cortices in freely moving rats following acute administration of the potent synthetic cannabinoid 5F-EDMB-PICA (0.3 mg/kg, i.p.). RESULTS: 5F-EDMB-PICA significantly suppressed low- (30-49 Hz) and high-gamma (51-80 Hz) power in PrL and MD, with a transient low-gamma reduction in OFC, while increasing long-range gamma coherence between the MD and prefrontal regions in both sub-bands. Notably, the drug increased the occurrence of high‑voltage spindles (HVS, 6-12 Hz) recorded in the MD, and enhanced phase-amplitude coupling between the phase of both HVS and theta (4-8 Hz) and the amplitude of prefrontal gamma. CONCLUSIONS: These results reveal that acute synthetic cannabinoid exposure produces a dissociation between local and long-range oscillatory dynamics in the thalamo-prefrontal circuit, which possibly is driven by increased thalamic rhythmic output. This pattern of network reorganization may underlie cannabinoid-induced deficits in sensorimotor gating and cognitive integration.

articles.title: Beyond psychedelic exceptionalism: how people combine meditation with psychoactive substances, and how this relates to well-being.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Combining meditation with psychoactive substances is often assumed to be a niche practice centred on classic psychedelics. We sought to broaden this narrative in two cross-sectional studies. METHODS: Study 1 used a broad naturalistic sample (N = 1,391) to examine the prevalence of substance use, meditation, and their simultaneous combination, as well as associations with subjective happiness. Study 2 used a stratified subsample (n = 397) focusing on classic psychedelic and cannabis users, the most common psychedelic-type substances combined with meditation, to assess associations with mental well-being, peace of mind, psychological flexibility, depression, and anxiety. RESULTS: Contrary to prevailing assumptions, alcohol (29%), cannabis (19%), and nicotine (16%) were far more commonly combined with meditation than classic psychedelics (6%). Classic psychedelic use was also embedded within a pattern of pronounced polysubstance use, suggesting that it may reflect a broader substance-use profile rather than an isolated behavioural practice. Regression analyses found no consistent associations between psychedelic or cannabis use, with or without meditation, and any outcome. However, an unexpected pattern emerged for other drugs and alcohol. Other- drug use without meditation was associated with poorer well-being outcomes relative to no other-drug use, whereas other-drug use combined with meditation was not. Alcohol combined with meditation was associated with better well-being outcomes relative to alcohol use without meditation. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that combining meditation with substance use is not limited to psychedelics and should be studied within broader patterns of polysubstance use and meditation practice.

articles.title: What goes up must comedown: prevalence rates, characteristics, and coping strategies concerning MDMA aftereffects.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: MDMA is increasingly being studied for therapeutic applications, yet the prevalence and characteristics of post-acute negative effects remain debated. OBJECTIVES: We aimed to characterize MDMA's post-acute negative effects, including prevalence and symptom profile among recreational users. Given preclinical work and limited human evidence suggesting that certain supplements and antidepressants may mitigate MDMA's negative effects, we also assessed the use of these substances as coping strategies. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional online survey of 497 MDMA-experienced participants recruited from Prolific. The survey assessed post-acute negative effects prevalence, timing, and duration; post-acute side effects; emotional changes, suicidal ideation; and intentional use of supplements or antidepressants to manage symptoms. We compared characteristics of post-acute side effects between MDMA users who self-reported ever experiencing a negative post-acute MDMA experience (colloquially known as a 'comedown') and those who did not. RESULTS: 74.5% of participants reported experiencing a period of post-acute negative effects at least once, with onset occurring approximately 24 hours post-ingestion and lasting an average of 40 hours. The most common symptoms were fatigue (88.1%), difficulty concentrating (85.7%), restlessness (82.9%), and headache (79.7%). 14.6% of post-acute negative effects experiencers endorsed passive suicidal ideation and 6.2% endorsed active suicidal ideation. Regarding coping strategies, 30.3% reported using supplements (most commonly N-acetyl-cysteine, acetyl-L-carnitine, and magnesium) and 5.1% reported using antidepressants, with moderate perceived helpfulness. CONCLUSIONS: Post-acute negative effects of MDMA appear prevalent among recreational users in a cross-sectional sample, characterized by fatigue, negative affect, and elevated suicidal ideation. These findings highlight post-acute risks that warrant further investigation.

articles.title: Serotonin 1B receptors expressed on forebrain excitatory neurons mediate the post-acute anxiolytic response to psilocybin in mice.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Psilocybin can produce rapid and sustained antidepressant-like and anxiolytic effects, yet the receptor and circuit mechanisms underlying these behavioral changes remain unclear. While the serotonin 2A receptor mediates psilocybin's acute psychedelic effects, psilocin (the active metabolite of psilocybin) binds many serotonin receptor subtypes. Our prior work has identified the serotonin 1B receptor (5-HT1BR) as being necessary for the post-acute pro-hedonic and anxiolytic effects of psilocybin in mice. 5-HT1BRs are widely expressed throughout the brain on many different neuron subtypes. METHODS: In order to assess the role of 5-HT1BR expression on terminals of forebrain excitatory neurons in the response to psilocybin, we used a conditional genetic approach to selectively eliminate expression of htr1b in forebrain excitatory neurons using the Emx1 promoter. We examined acute behavioral responses, post-acute anxiolytic effects, and brain-wide neural activation to a single high dose of psilocybin in male and female mice. RESULTS: The absence of 5-HT1BR expression on Emx1+ neurons did not alter psilocybin's acute behavioral effects, including head twitch responding and hyperlocomotion. However, psilocybin's post-acute anxiolytic effects in the elevated plus maze (EPM) and novelty suppressed feeding (NSF) assays were strongly attenuated in mice lacking these receptors. Whole-brain c-Fos mapping across 190 regions revealed that psilocybin produced robust activation across the brain in both genotypes, including prefrontal cortices, corticolimbic structures, and sensory cortices. Network-level analyses revealed that psilocybin drove broad inter-regional decorrelation in control mice but increased synchronization in knockouts, with thalamic, prefrontal, and amygdala circuits most strongly affected. CONCLUSIONS: These findings implicate 5-HT1BRs expressed on terminals of forebrain excitatory neurons as a potential circuit-level excitatory gating mechanism. Overall, these receptors may be important for a coordinated network reorganization following psilocybin that contributes to the anxiolytic behavioral effects.

articles.title: Health technology assessment of long-acting erythropoiesis-stimulating agents for the treatment of renal anemia in China.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Renal anemia is a common complication of chronic kidney disease (CKD) and is associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity and mortality and reduced quality of life. Long-acting erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) offer advantages in dosing convenience and adherence, but a comprehensive multidimensional evaluation comparing these agents within the Chinese healthcare context is lacking. OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to conduct a multidimensional quantitative evaluation of long-acting ESAs and provide a reference for drug selection and rational clinical use in medical institutions. METHODS: Based on the method recommended in the Rapid Guideline for Drug Evaluation and Selection in Chinese Medical Institutions (Third Edition), three long-acting ESAs were evaluated in five dimensions, namely, efficacy (28 points), safety (27 points), pharmaceutical properties (27 points), economy (10 points), and other attributes (8 points). RESULTS: The final assessment scores were 80.39 points for the continuous erythropoietin receptor activator (CERA), 73.04 points for pegmolesatide, and 71.70 points for darbepoetin alfa, in descending order. CERA achieved the highest scores in safety and other attributes, darbepoetin alfa ranked first in economy, and pegmolesatide performed best in pharmaceutical properties. CONCLUSION: According to the scoring results, CERA, pegmolesatide, and darbepoetin alfa all exceeded the guideline-defined threshold for strong recommendation (>70 points) and can be included in the list of strongly recommended drugs for medical institutions. This study provides a scientific, reasonable, and safe basis for medical institutions to select long-acting ESAs.

articles.title: Genotoxic evaluation of chemical fractions of Cymbopogon citratus (DC) Stapf using plasmid assay.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cymbopogon citratus (DC.) Stapf is a medicinal plant widely used in traditional medicine in Africa, Asia and Latin America, mainly consumed as aqueous decoctions or infusions to treat fever, colds, cough, gastrointestinal disorders, hypertension, inflammation and anxiety. Despite its extensive traditional use, information on the genotoxic and oxidative effects of its individual chemical fractions remains limited. METHODS: The DNA strand breaks and oxidative effects of the aqueous, butanolic and essential oil fractions obtained from the aqueous extract of C. citratus were evaluated using an ex vivo purified pCMUT plasmid DNA model. Cleavage was analyzed after short- and long-term exposure, and oxidative damage was assessed using formamidopyrimidine-DNA glycosylase (FPG). Phytochemical characterization of the aqueous and butanolic fractions was performed by HPLC-HR-MS/MS. RESULTS: None of the fractions induced plasmid cleavage after 30 min of exposure. However, the aqueous fraction caused significant DNA strand breaks after prolonged incubation. Oxidative DNA damage was detected with the aqueous and essential oil fractions, whereas the butanolic fraction showed no detectable oxidative or breaking effects. Phytochemical analysis revealed qualitative and quantitative differences between fractions, particularly in phenolic acids and flavonoids. DISCUSSION: The aqueous fraction of C. citratus exhibits a higher genotoxic and pro-oxidant potential under prolonged exposure, while the butanolic fraction presents a safer profile under the evaluated conditions. These findings highlight the importance of fraction-specific toxicological assessment to support the safe traditional and pharmacological use of C. citratus.

articles.title: Ginsenoside Rb1 ameliorates stress urinary incontinence by upregulating SIRT1 to preserve mitochondrial homeostasis and MAM integrity.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Stress urinary incontinence (SUI) is a prevalent pelvic floor disorder characterized by impaired connective tissue integrity. Oxidative stress-induced mitochondrial dysfunction has been implicated in pelvic floor degeneration. Ginsenoside Rb1 (Rb1), a bioactive component of ginseng, exhibits antioxidant properties; however, its therapeutic effects and underlying mechanisms in SUI remain unclear. METHODS: A vaginal distension (VD)-induced mouse model of SUI and an H2O2-induced oxidative stress model in L929 cells were established to investigate the effects of Rb1. Urodynamic evaluation, histological analysis, mitochondrial functional assays, and SIRT1 inhibition/knockdown experiments were performed to explore the molecular mechanisms. RESULTS: Rb1 significantly improved bladder leak point pressure, preserved collagen organization, and reduced apoptosis in the anterior vaginal wall of VD mice. Rb1 alleviated oxidative stress by reducing ROS accumulation and restoring mitochondrial homeostasis. Mechanistically, Rb1 upregulated SIRT1 and enhanced mitochondrial biogenesis-associated signaling through the PGC-1α/NRF1/TFAM pathway, while promoting PINK1/Parkin-associated mitophagic signaling. Furthermore, Rb1 maintained mitochondria-associated membrane (MAM) integrity by regulating GRP75 acetylation, thereby reducing excessive ER-mitochondrial calcium transfer, mitochondrial calcium overload, and mtROS accumulation. SIRT1 inhibition or knockdown attenuated these protective effects. CONCLUSION: Ginsenoside Rb1 protects against SUI by promoting SIRT1-associated mitochondrial quality control and preserving MAM homeostasis through regulation of GRP75 acetylation. These findings identify the SIRT1-GRP75/MAM axis as a potential therapeutic target for preventing oxidative stress-induced pelvic floor tissue dysfunction.

articles.title: Dendrobine's mechanism: alleviating cholesterol metabolism disorders via FXR/LXR modulation in NAFLD mouse livers.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cholesterol homeostasis is tightly regulated through hepatic synthesis, intestinal absorption, and biliary excretion, with bile acids serving as critical regulators of cholesterol catabolism. Dysregulated cholesterol metabolism and bile acid imbalance are hallmarks of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), contributing to hepatic lipid accumulation and disease progression. Dendrobine (DNE), a bioactive alkaloid from Dendrobium nobile, has emerged as a potential therapeutic candidate for lipid metabolic disorders. METHODS: C57BL/6J mice were fed a high-fat diet to establish an NAFLD model, followed by DNE administration. Hepatic steatosis and cholesterol deposition were evaluated via histology and biochemical assays; bile acid profiles were quantified by LC-MS/MS. Gene and protein expression were analyzed using RT-qPCR and Western blotting. In vitro studies using cholesterol-laden HepG2 cells further explored DNE's mechanisms, validated by specific pharmacological agonists and inhibitors of the Farnesoid X receptor (FXR) and liver X receptor (LXR) pathways. RESULTS: DNE significantly ameliorated hepatic steatosis and reduced cholesterol accumulation in HFD-induced NAFLD mice. LC-MS/MS analysis revealed that DNE substantially expanded the bile acid (BA) pool in the liver, bile, and ileum. Mechanistically, DNE comprehensively modulated cholesterol absorption, biotransformation, and transport by modulating the FXR and LXR signaling pathways. It robustly upregulated key genes involved in BA synthesis (e.g., Cyp7a1) and efflux, while downregulating transporters responsible for BA and cholesterol reuptake (e.g., Ntcp, Npc1l1). In vitro validation using specific pharmacological agonists and antagonists further confirmed that DNE upregulates CYP7A1 and promotes BA synthesis via a dual FXR/LXRα-dependent regulatory network. CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that DNE modulates cholesterol homeostasis and alleviates NAFLD in conjunction with BA synthesis, transport, and absorption, in a manner associated with the FXR/LXRα regulatory network, presenting a promising therapeutic strategy.

articles.title: microRNA-15b modulates stress-induced premature senescence in chronic doxorubicin cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Doxorubicin (DOX) is the most widely used anthracycline in hematologic and solid tumors, whose clinical utility is constrained by dose-dependent cumulative cardiotoxicity that can progress to chronic heart failure. Although previously attributed to overt cardiomyocyte loss, emerging evidence indicates that stress-induced premature senescence (SIPS) constitutes the dominant mechanism of chronic cardiotoxicity at clinically relevant concentrations. SIPS is defined by permanent cell cycle arrest, activation of the p53/p21 and p16/Rb tumor suppressor axes, mitochondrial dysfunction, and a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) that sustains a pro-inflammatory myocardial milieu. Nevertheless, the post-transcriptional mechanisms that govern this process remain incompletely understood. METHODS: The post-transcriptional regulation of DOX-induced SIPS was evaluated in vitro using neonatal rat ventricular myocytes (NRVMs) exposed to sublethal DOX (0.1 μM) with or without prophylactic miR-15b restoration via a synthetic mimetic to assess the p53/p21, p16, SASP, lysosomal, and mitochondrial responses. In vivo, a chronic cardiotoxicity model was established in female C57BL/6 mice receiving a cumulative dose of 30 mg/kg DOX to analyze myocardial miR-15b suppression, SIPS markers, and SASP profiles across survival cohorts. RESULTS: Sublethal DOX treatment (0.1 μM) suppressed miR-15b expression by approximately 50% in NRVMs, resulting in post-transcriptional derepression of its mitochondrial target, SIRT4. This miR-15b loss triggered a multiparametric SIPS phenotype encompassing accumulation of γH2AX foci, p53/p21 and p16 activation, SASP induction (IL-6, IL-1β, Mcp-1 and Mmp13), lysosomal dysfunction (increased SA-β-Gal staining) and mitochondrial dysfunction. Prophylactic restoration of miR-15b via a synthetic mimetic selectively attenuated the p53/p21 axis, genomic damage foci, lysosomal dysfunction, mitochondrial dysfunction and SASP (IL-6 and IL-1β), without rescuing the p16/Rb pathway. In the female C57BL/6 chronic cardiotoxicity model, the cohort spontaneously stratified into animals completing the protocol (ND; 67%) and a premature death subgroup (PD; 33%). The PD subgroup exhibited the most profound myocardial miR-15b suppression and greater accumulation of SIPS markers, including γH2AX, p16, and reduced Lamin B. Notably, the SASP displayed distinct qualitative profiles between PD and ND animals, suggesting that SASP composition, rather than magnitude alone, determines the cardiotoxic outcome. CONCLUSION: Collectively, these findings position miR-15b as a key post-transcriptional regulator of DOX-induced SIPS in the cardiomyocyte, whose sustained loss associates with cardiotoxicity severity in vivo.

articles.title: In vitro pharmacological profiling of ITE amide bioisosteric aryl hydrocarbon receptor agonist.
articles.abstract: Previously, we reported ITE-derived bioisostere 2-(1H-indole-3-carbonyl)-N-methyl thiazole-4-carboxamide (ITE-CONHCH3) as a high-affinity ligand and potent agonist of the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) with anti-colitis properties. In the current study, we present its initial in vitro pharmacological profiling. Physicochemical analysis revealed low aqueous solubility (22 µM), excellent chemical stability in human and mouse plasma, and strong plasma protein binding (>98%). Off-target screening against steroid and nuclear receptors confirmed high AhR selectivity. In Caco-2 cells, ITE-CONHCH3 exhibited high permeability with no active efflux. Interestingly, the compound partitioned substantially into mouse red blood cells (47%) but only weakly into human RBCs (16%). In reporter gene assays, ITE-CONHCH3 displayed ∼40-fold higher agonist potency in human cells compared to mouse cells. Its ability to activate AhR was further validated by a cell-free AhR-ARNT heterodimerization assay and by the induction of canonical (CYP1A1) and non-canonical (PAI-1) genes expression in Caco-2 cells. In conclusion, ITE-CONHCH3 possesses a favorable pharmacological profile supporting its potential preclinical development. However, the observed differences in RBC partitioning and AhR potency between species must be considered when interpreting mouse-derived data.

articles.title: Risk of hyperglycemia with different statins by type and dose: a network meta-analysis and real-world pharmacovigilance study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The potential diabetogenic effects of statins remain controversial, particularly with respect to differences across statin types and doses. METHODS: We conducted a network meta-analysis (NMA) of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to assess the comparative effects of different statins and doses on hyperglycemia-related outcomes. The NMA was performed within a Bayesian framework. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov were systematically searched from inception to April 2025. Data extraction and verification were independently conducted by two investigators. Outcomes included risk of new-onset diabetes mellitus (NODM), fasting plasma glucose (FPG), 2-h postprandial plasma glucose, and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c). Separately, we conducted a real-world pharmacovigilance analysis using disproportionality methods based on the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) to identify potential hyperglycemia-related safety signals in patients without diabetes. RESULTS: A total of 22 RCTs, which enrolled 99,311 patients, were included. The NMA found no statistically significant differences in NODM risk among statins or compared with placebo. However, pravastatin 40 mg/day showed a numerically lower risk estimate (OR: 0.86; 95% CrI: 0.50-1.50), whereas rosuvastatin 20 mg/day and atorvastatin 80 mg/day showed relatively higher estimates. Analyses of intermediate glycemic markers, including FPG and HbA1c, revealed no significant differences across all statin regimens and placebo. In parallel, FAERS pharmacovigilance analyses identified disproportionate reporting signals for hyperglycemic events with atorvastatin (ROR: 6.11; 95% CI: 5.94-6.29), rosuvastatin (ROR: 2.44; 95% CI: 2.31-2.58), and simvastatin (ROR: 1.22; 95% CI: 1.13-1.32). CONCLUSION: No statistically significant differences in glycemic outcomes were observed among individual statins or compared with placebo. However, numerical variations in point estimates across randomized evidence and pharmacovigilance signals suggest possible differences in glycemic profiles among statins. Pravastatin showed numerically lower risk estimates; however, these findings were accompanied by substantial uncertainty. Further prospective studies are needed to clarify these observations.

articles.title: Shenze shugan capsules alleviate alcoholic liver injury in association with modulation of the TGF-β/smad4 signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) represents a major contributor to liver fibrosis globally, and current therapeutic options remain inadequate. The TGF-β/Smad4 cascade is critically involved in alcohol-evoked activation of hepatic stellate cells and subsequent extracellular matrix accumulation. Although Shenze Shugan capsule (SZSG) has been clinically used for non-alcoholic steatohepatitis, its efficacy and mechanisms in ALD are unclear. This study aimed to explore how SZSG exerts protective effects against alcohol-triggered liver injury and the underlying mechanisms. METHODS: Both acute and chronic ALD mouse models were established to assess liver injury, fibrosis, inflammation, gut microbiota composition, and serum metabolomic profiles. RESULTS: SZSG treatment markedly attenuated hepatic steatosis, fibrosis, and inflammation, as evidenced by reductions in lipid accumulation, collagen deposition, and pro-inflammatory cytokine levels. Concurrently, it reshaped the gut microbiota and restored metabolites dysregulated by alcohol exposure. These beneficial effects appear to involve modulation of the TGF-β/Smad4 signaling pathway and its downstream effectors, α-SMA and Collagen I. CONCLUSION: Collectively, our findings suggest that SZSG combats ALD by simultaneously modulating the TGF-β/Smad4 signaling axis and preserving gut-liver homeostasis, thereby representing a promising multi-target therapeutic candidate.

articles.title: hsa_circ_0001377 promotes hepatic fibrosis by sponging let-7a-5p and targeting TGFBR1, Smad2, and Col1a2.
articles.abstract: Background: Hepatic fibrosis (HF) is primarily driven by the activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) and is characterized by excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) accumulation. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have recently gained increasing attention in HF research. Methods: RNA sequencing and bioinformatic analyses revealed elevated hsa_circ_0001377 expression in human HF tissues. Its circular structure and subcellular localization were identified using Sanger sequencing, RNase R treatment, and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH). Gain- and loss-of-function experiments were conducted to elucidate the role of hsa_circ_0001377 in the human HSC line LX-2. Furthermore, the in vitro and in vivo effects of the hsa_circ_0001377/let-7a-5p/TGFBR1, Smad2, and Col1a2 regulatory axis were investigated using cytological assays and a bile duct ligation (BDL)-induced mouse model of HF. Results: hsa_circ_0001377 was significantly upregulated in the circRNA expression profile of human HF tissues. Its circular structure was validated through Sanger sequencing and resistance to RNase R digestion. FISH and co-staining with α-SMA demonstrated that hsa_circ_0001377 was abundantly expressed in activated HSCs (aHSCs; α-SMA-positive cells). Gain- and loss-of-function assays were performed using LX-2 cells with stable hsa_circ_0001377 overexpression and a specific siRNA targeting this circRNA. hsa_circ_0001377 overexpression promoted LX-2 cell activation, proliferation, migration, and G1/S-phase transition, whereas its knockdown produced the opposite effects. qRT-PCR, AGO-RIP, dual-luciferase reporter, and miRNA pulldown assays confirmed that hsa_circ_0001377 acts as a molecular sponge for let-7a-5p and that let-7a-5p targets TGFBR1, Smad2, and Col1a2. Rescue experiments in LX-2 cells further demonstrated that hsa_circ_0001377 promotes HSC activation, proliferation, migration, and G1/S-phase transition through the let-7a-5p/TGFBR1, Smad2, and Col1a2 axis. Moreover, hsa_circ_0001377 was highly expressed in 20 human HF samples, and its expression increased with advancing fibrosis stage. In vivo, a BDL-induced murine HF model demonstrated that the homologous mmu_circ_0001377 was also significantly upregulated in fibrotic liver tissues. In addition, tail-vein injection of an mmu-let-7a-5p agomir into BDL-induced HF mice confirmed the inhibitory effects of the let-7a-5p/TGFBR1, Smad2, and Col1a2 axis on α-SMA expression and collagen deposition. Conclusion: Taken together, these findings suggest that the hsa_circ_0001377/let-7a-5p/TGFBR1, Smad2, and Col1a2 regulatory axis may represent a promising therapeutic target for HF.

articles.title: Solanidine metabolic ratios for CYP2D6 phenotyping after a standardized potato meal.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The recent identification of the diet-derived CYP2D6 biomarker solanidine, a potato constituent, enables the study of CYP2D6 activity in vivo. Although solanidine metabolic ratios (MR) were shown to be relatively stable over the day with high positive correlations to CYP2D6 phenotype and genotype, the influence of a solanidine-containing potato meal on solanidine metabolite plasma concentrations and MR is unclear. METHODS: In this study with 20 healthy participants, not preselected for specific CYP2D6 genotypes, a standardized potato meal was administered after 3 days of potato-fasting (DRKS00031441). Blood sampling was conducted at 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 29 h. Participants were genotyped for CYP2D6 and plasma concentrations of solanidine and its metabolites 4-OH-solanidine and 3,4-secosolanidine-3,4-dioic acid (SSDA) were measured by LC-MS/MS. MRs were formed by dividing metabolite by substrate concentrations at each sampling time point. RESULTS: Solanidine and metabolite plasma concentrations showed no consistent increases. Solanidine plasma concentrations (29 h vs. baseline) increased in median 0.09 ng/mL (range: -0.37 to 1.43 ng/mL). Within the period of 29 h, the linear relationship of solanidine ln MRs to the CYP2D6 activity score (AS) improved over time after intake of the potato meal with the best association after 29 h (r2 = 0.56). DISCUSSION: Changes in solanidine and metabolite plasma concentrations after the potato meal were variable, which could be attributed to interindividual absorption variability. CYP2D6 phenotyping may be improved by a previous potato meal at least 1 day before blood sampling. This may allow solanidine CYP2D6 phenotyping in populations with low dietary potato consumption.

articles.title: Impact of seven conservation methods on the nutritional value, phytochemical composition, and chemical antioxidant capacity of Terfezia boudieri and Tirmania nivea from Southeastern Tunisia.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Desert truffles (Terfezia boudieri and Tirmania nivea) are edible fungi valued for their nutritional and nutraceutical properties. However, the effects of post-harvest preservation on their bioactive composition and health-related quality remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the influence of seven conservation methods on the nutritional and functional properties of both species collected from the arid regions of southeastern Tunisia. METHODS: Seven preservation techniques (sun drying, oven drying, deep freezing, lyophilization, chips processing, marination, and olive-oil preservation) were assessed. Nutritional composition, mineral content, vitamins, carotenoids, phenolic compounds, and antioxidant activity were determined using standard analytical methods. Data were analyzed by two-way ANOVA to evaluate the effects of preservation method, species, and their interaction. RESULTS: Preservation method was the main source of variation, explaining up to 99.06% of protein, 95.65% of carbohydrate, 94.88% of antioxidant activity, 88.19% of potassium, and 87.07% of total phenolic variability (all P < 0.0001), whereas species effects were comparatively minor. Oven drying and lyophilization best preserved protein content (≈27-28%) and antioxidant activity (87-89% radical scavenging activity). Lyophilization and marination retained the highest mineral concentrations, while lyophilization also preserved the greatest riboflavin (2.69-3.94 ppm) and lycopene (0.15-0.16 ppm) contents. Oven drying produced the highest phenolic acid levels, whereas chips processing consistently reduced proteins, minerals, vitamins, and bioactive compounds. DISCUSSION: Preservation method is the principal determinant of the nutritional and nutraceutical quality of desert truffles. Oven drying and lyophilization were the most effective strategies for maintaining health-promoting compounds, supporting their application as optimal post-harvest technologies to maximize the functional food value and commercial potential of T. boudieri and T. nivea.

articles.title: Wild ginseng adventitious roots restore sleep homeostasis in sleep-deprived Drosophila melanogaster.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Sleep deprivation is increasingly recognized as a major health concern and is associated with impaired physiological and neurological functions. Panax ginseng C. A. Mey. has long been used to improve sleep quality; however, the limited availability and long cultivation cycle of natural ginseng restrict its sustainable utilization. Wild ginseng adventitious roots (ADV), produced via plant tissue culture, provide a renewable source of bioactive ginsenosides, although their potential role in sleep regulation remains poorly understood. METHODS: The sleep-promoting effects and safety of ADV were evaluated in a sleep deprivation-induced Drosophila melanogaster model. Sleep parameters, including total sleep duration, sleep latency, deep sleep, and sleep fragmentation, were assessed, together with addiction-like behavioral assays. Transcriptomic analysis was performed to investigate the underlying mechanisms. LC-MS/MS and bioactivity assays were conducted to identify and validate major active ginsenosides. RESULTS: ADV significantly improved sleep behavior in sleep-deprived flies, increasing total sleep duration and deep sleep while reducing sleep latency and sleep fragmentation, without inducing addiction-like behaviors. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that ADV modulated multiple sleep-related biological processes, particularly stress response pathway, as evidenced by altered expression of Hsp68, Hsp70Aa, Hsp70Ba, Hsp70Bb, and Hsp70Bbb. Combined with LC-MS/MS identification and biological activity comparison, ginsenosides Rc and F2 were preliminarily identified as the principal active metabolites. CONCLUSION: In the Drosophila melanogaster sleep-deprivation model, ADV treatment is associated with improvements in sleep-related behavioural parameters alongside altered expression of conserved stress-response-related biological processes. These findings support ADV as a sustainable source of bioactive ginsenosides, though the current experimental design cannot establish a strictly sleep-specific or causal mechanistic relationship.

articles.title: Resolvin D1 attenuates pulmonary hypertension by suppressing pathological connexin 43-mediated gap junctional communication in pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is characterized by progressive pulmonary vascular remodeling driven by activation of pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs). Resolvin D1 (RvD1), a specialized pro-resolving lipid mediator derived from docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), has vascular protective actions; however, its pharmacological effect on connexin 43 (Cx43)-mediated gap junctional intercellular communication in PH remains unclear. This study investigated whether RvD1 attenuates PH by suppressing pathological formation of gap-junctional Cx43 (GJs-Cx43) in PASMCs. METHODS: SU5416/hypoxia-induced PH was established in C57BL/6 mice. In vitro, primary mouse PASMCs were cultured under hypoxic conditions to mimic the hypoxic pathological microenvironment and PASMCs activation associated with PH. Pulmonary hemodynamics, right ventricular function and hypertrophy, pulmonary arterial remodeling, and Cx43 distribution in isolated small pulmonary arteries were evaluated in vivo. In PASMCs, biochemical fractionation, Western blotting, immunofluorescence, lucifer yellow dye transfer, cell proliferation and migration assays, and inflammatory and oxidative stress assessments were performed. ZP1609 was used to enhance GJs-Cx43 function in vitro and in vivo. RESULTS: RvD1 improved pulmonary hemodynamics and right ventricular adaptation in SU5416/hypoxia-exposed mice. RvD1 also reduced pulmonary arterial wall thickening, elastic lamina remodeling, α-SMA accumulation and PCNA-positive proliferating cells. Mechanistically, SU5416/hypoxia increased total Cx43 and shifted Cx43 toward the GJs-Cx43 formation. RvD1 inhibited GJs-Cx43 formation and attenuated IL-1β, IL-6, ROS and MDA accumulation while partially restoring SOD. In primary PASMCs, hypoxia increased GJs-Cx43 expression, enhanced lucifer yellow dye transfer, and promoted proliferation and migration; these changes were suppressed by RvD1. ZP1609 restored GJs-Cx43-mediated intercellular communication and weakened the inhibitory effects of RvD1 on PASMC inflammatory activation, oxidative stress, proliferation and migration. In vivo, ZP1609 similarly blunted the protection conferred by RvD1 against pulmonary vascular remodeling, right ventricular pressure overload and right ventricular hypertrophy. CONCLUSION: Pathological GJs-Cx43 formation promotes the spread of remodeling-associated signals across PASMCs networks. RvD1 limits pulmonary vascular remodeling by suppressing Cx43-dependent gap junctional communication, identifying GJs-Cx43 as a pharmacologically relevant mechanism underlying the vascular protection afforded by this DHA-derived lipid mediator.

articles.title: Mechanistic mass transport analysis of dissolution of weak-base drugs considering the influence of surface pH in formulations with and without acidifying agents.
articles.abstract: At the solid-liquid interface, the dissolution of weakly basic drugs, particularly those exhibiting poor solubility, is highly sensitive to local pH conditions. These compounds frequently show pH-dependent solubility and reduced bioavailability when co-administered with acid-reducing agents, which presents significant difficulties for formulation design and clinical efficacy. Despite advances in physiologically based biopharmaceutics modeling, most existing dissolution modeling frameworks fail to account for microenvironmental pH changes induced by functional excipients such as acidifying or basifying agents. To address this critical gap, we developed a mechanistic mass-transport-based dissolution framework that explicitly quantifies surface pH as a function of excipient diffusion and acid-base equilibria. The model integrates coupled diffusion-reaction kinetics within the diffusion boundary layer, enabling accurate prediction of interfacial pH under both buffered and unbuffered conditions. Building on the classical framework, we numerically captured the impact of monoprotic and diprotic acidifying agents on surface pH. Model validation was performed using entrectinib, a clinically relevant weak base, across formulations with and without acidifying agents, supported by experimental dissolution data generated under different media conditions. The results demonstrate that bulk pH-based modeling is insufficient to capture critical formulation-driven dissolution behavior and establish surface pH as a primary determinant of dissolution kinetics. Overall, this study establishes surface pH modeling as a key advancement for mechanistic dissolution prediction of oral drug products containing functional pH-modifying excipients.

articles.title: Self-reported prescription medication use and polypharmacy following physical combat injury in the UK: the ADVANCE cohort study.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The consequences of serious physical traumatic injury may require pharmacological intervention, however long-term use and polypharmacy can increase risk of morbidity/mortality. This study aims to describe prescription medication use in a cohort of UK Armed Forces personnel who sustained physical combat injuries during the Afghanistan conflict (injured group) compared to demographically similar personnel without such injuries (uninjured group) a median of 11 years post injury. METHODS: One thousand and fifty one participants of the ADVANCE cohort (injured group n = 526 uninjured group n = 525), including individuals with (n = 141) and without (n = 384) limb loss or with (n = 226) and without (n = 300) deployment-related Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI), reported medication use during a clinical interview. Overall incidence of prescribing any medication, specific anatomical/therapeutic classes (e.g., Central Nervous System (CNS), psychotropic or analgesic) and medications with pain or mental health indications were investigated. General (≥5 medications), CNS (≥5), psychotropic (≥2) and analgesic (≥2) polypharmacy was also investigated. RESULTS: Compared to the uninjured group, the injured group reported a greater prevalence of prescription medication use (17.8% vs. 29.7%), including medications acting on the CNS (8.0% vs. 17.2%), psychotropics (6.3% vs. 11.8%) and analgesics (2.2% vs. 8.6%). Prevalence of polypharmacy was very low in the cohort (0%-4.4%). Incidence Rate Ratios (IRR) and 95% confidence intervals indicated that injured personnel were currently using on average over twice as many prescription medications as those in the uninjured group (IRR 2.15 (1.66, 2.92)), including medications acting on the CNS (IRR 2.67 (1.77, 4.08)), and psychotropics (IRR 2.03 (1.27, 3.25)). Similar elevations were present in those injured with and without limb loss and especially elevated in those with deployment-related TBI. Use of psychotropics amongst personnel injured with limb loss were predominantly for non-mental health indications (e.g., sleep, pain). CONCLUSION: Pharmacological intervention is not uncommon amongst UK Armed Forces personnel who sustained serious physical injuries, but the prevalence of polypharmacy is low. Effective prescribing practices should ensure optimal recovery whilst minimising the risk of adverse events.

articles.title: Gastrodin inhibits neuronal ferroptosis by regulating mir-455-5p/ACSL4 pathway after stroke via exosome.
articles.abstract: Recent studies have demonstrated that ferroptosis plays a crucial role in neuronal cell death following cerebral infarction. Our previous research showed that gastrodin (GAS) significantly improved neurological function in rats subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO); however, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In the present study, we employed Western blotting, quantitative PCR (qPCR), and immunofluorescence assays to investigate the changes in the expression levels of ferroptosis-related regulatory proteins (ACSL4, TFR1, GPX4, and MBL-2) in both in vivo and in vitro models following ischemic-hypoxic injury, as well as the modulatory effects of gastrodin on these proteins. We also conducted an in-depth exploration of an innovative therapeutic approach involving exosomes. Specifically, we constructed gastrodin-treated serum exosomes (GSE) to assess their role in neuroprotection. Our findings revealed that gastrodin significantly reduced infarct volume in middle cerebral artery occlusion rats. Compared with the model group, the levels of ACSL4, TFR1, and MBL-2 proteins were markedly decreased, while GPX4 expression was significantly upregulated in the ischemic hemisphere of the gastrodin-treated rats. These results suggest that gastrodin exerts neuroprotective effects by inhibiting ferroptosis following cerebral infarction. In an oxygen-glucose deprivation model using Neuro-2a cells, we further observed that GSE enhanced cell viability by suppressing ferroptosis. Using RNA immunoprecipitation dual-luciferase reporter assays, and fluorescence in situ hybridization we confirmed colocalization between miR-455-5p and ACSL4. Subsequently, we manipulated miR-455-5p expression in Neuro-2a cells through transfection and assessed cell viability using CCK-8 and Live/Dead assays. The results demonstrated that GSE inhibited OGD-induced ferroptosis and improved cell viability by modulating the miR-455-5p/ACSL4 signaling pathway. In conclusion, our study indicates that gastrodin can suppress neuronal ferroptosis probably through an exosome-mediated mechanism involving the miR-455-5p/ACSL4 pathway, thereby exerting neuroprotective effects after ischemic injury. In addition, exosomal delivery represents a promising strategy to treat stroke.

articles.title: Timing dictates efficacy: evaluating the prophylactic and therapeutic potential of dimethyl fumarate against LPS-induced shock.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a serious and often fatal condition that is caused by endotoxemia as a result of systemic inflammation and uncontrolled oxidative stress. Although dimethyl fumarate (DMF) has shown to have immunomodulatory and antioxidant activity, its specific prophylactic and therapeutic activity in endotoxemia-induced AKI remains unclear. AIM: to study DMF's effect on endotoxemia-induced AKI in a mouse in vivo model. METHODS: We divided the mice (Swiss albino) into eight equal groups. The endotoxemia-induced AKI was treated by intraperitoneal injection with LPS (5 mg/kg). Prophylactic cohorts received oral DMF (50 or 100 mg/kg/day) for three consecutive days prior to the challenge. Therapeutic cohorts were given a single DMF dose one hour after the treatment. At six hours, gross renal function (BUN, creatinine), cytokine levels, Nrf2/HO-1 activation, oxidative damage biomarkers, inflammasome/apoptotic pathways and acute tubular necrosis (ATN) histopathology were assessed. RESULTS: LPS challenge resulted in severe renal dysfunction, the onset of a massive cytokine storm and acute tubular destruction. The pre-treatment of DMF prevented the TLR4/NF-κB inflammatory pathway and the overall renal cytoarchitecture was preserved. On the other hand, therapeutic DMF demonstrated a unique anti-inflammatory "ceiling effect" where both low and high doses inhibited NF-κB activation. Therapeutic DMF was more robust in structural and functional rescue, upregulating the Nrf2/HO-1 defense axis, neutralizing reactive oxygen species, and blocking the final inflammasome priming and pyroptotic actions. CONCLUSION: The timing of intervention fundamentally dictates pharmacological efficacy. Prophylaxis offers strong preventative shielding, whereas high-dose therapeutic DMF successfully mitigates ongoing oxidative storms, providing a compelling and highly translatable rationale for clinical repurposing in critical care nephrology.

articles.title: Pharmacometabolomic signatures as individualised biochemical response evidence: towards a precision jurisprudence framework for forensic toxicology and criminal responsibility.
articles.abstract: Precision medicine is transforming drug response from a population level assumption into an individualised biochemical event. Pharmacometabolomics, which profiles metabolic signatures associated with drug exposure and response, offers a mechanistic basis for explaining interindividual variability in therapeutic efficacy, adverse drug reactions, neurocognitive impairment and toxicological ambiguity. Legal systems, however, continue to evaluate drug related conduct largely through conventional toxicology, generalised impairment thresholds and binary assumptions about intent, voluntariness and negligence. This Perspective proposes individualised biochemical response evidence, described here metaphorically as an emerging category of biochemical legal identity, as a prospective research and governance framework rather than a validated evidentiary standard. Its primary focus is forensic toxicology and criminal responsibility, with medical negligence, product liability, AI guided prescribing, pharmaceutical regulation and biochemical privacy discussed as secondary implications requiring separate validation. The claim is not that metabolomic profiles are currently capable of establishing individual causation, voluntariness or capacity, but that a disciplined evidentiary pathway, moving from biological plausibility through analytical validity, clinical validity and forensic validity to legal admissibility, would be required before such evidence could inform these determinations. A precision jurisprudence framework is proposed to guide this transition while preserving safeguards against biochemical determinism, privacy intrusion and algorithmic opacity.

articles.title: CGRP remodels the acidic microenvironment and promotes pancreatic carcinoma progression by regulating NHE1 and CA9.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Neurons can regulate cancer cells to modulate their survival and growth, the interplay between calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) and the acidic tumor microenvironment (TME) in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains unknown. METHODS AND RESULTS: Here, we reported that CGRP expression and neuronal activation markers p-ERK/p-CREB were significantly elevated in PDAC tissues. Exogenous CGRP promoted PANC02 cell proliferation and migration, whereas CGRP knockout suppressed orthotopic tumor growth. Mechanistically, CGRP upregulated the proton transporters NHE1 and CA9, facilitating H+ efflux and reducing extracellular pH, thereby exacerbating TME acidification. Clinical analysis revealed that high expression of NHE1 and CA9 correlated with poor prognosis in PDAC patients. Rimegepant, a CGRP receptor antagonist, inhibited orthotopic tumor growth and exhibited synergistic effects with gemcitabine. CONCLUSION AND DISCUSSION: In conclusion, our findings uncover a functional connection between CGRPergic sensory neurons and the acidic TME, identifying the CGRP signaling pathway as a potential therapeutic target for PDAC. Despite these findings, the mechanistic conclusions remain correlative and require further validation, and the generalizability to human PDAC warrants future investigation.

articles.title: Hereditary angioedema in Latin America: international recommendations, expert consensus, and reported implementation barriers.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Current international hereditary angioedema (HAE) guidelines and treat-to-target recommendations emphasize accurate diagnosis, early on-demand treatment, procedure-related short-term prophylaxis, individualized long-term prophylaxis (LTP), and routine assessment of disease control and quality of life. Evidence on implementation in Latin America remains limited. We aimed to assess concordance between international guidance and the consensus of a selected Latin American expert panel and to identify expert-reported implementation barriers. METHODS: A scientific committee developed and externally validated a 74-item questionnaire (domains summarized in Supplementary Table S1) and conducted a two-round Delphi process among Latin American HAE experts. Consensus items were rated on a nine-point agreement scale, with consensus defined a priori as at least two-thirds of respondents scoring within a three-point band in the agreement or disagreement range. Descriptive items captured expert-reported diagnostic testing, treatment patterns, monitoring practices, and perceived implementation determinants. Consensus findings are summarized as meeting the prespecified threshold; descriptive findings are reported with item-specific n/N when available. Instrument validation (July-November 2024) showed high inter-rater agreement (Kendall W = 0.84; p < 0.001) and excellent internal consistency (Cronbach alpha = 0.92). RESULTS: Thirty experts from 10 countries completed the process (Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Mexico, Panama, Peru, Uruguay, and Venezuela). The prespecified consensus threshold was met for core biochemical diagnostic work-up, selective genetic evaluation, first-line targeted LTP (pdC1-INH, lanadelumab, and berotralstat), continued availability of on-demand therapy, routine monitoring, and management of special populations. The principal expert-reported implementation signal was limited feasibility: frequent or constant prophylaxis-supply interruptions were reported by 19/30 experts (63%), including 13/23 (57%) practicing in settings where public or insurance coverage was reported. Cost (19/30; 63%) and medicine availability (8/30; 27%) were the most frequently reported barriers. These reports were not independently verified against reimbursement, procurement, formulary, or inventory data. CONCLUSION: Within this selected panel, expert consensus was broadly concordant with international HAE guidance. Panelists reported barriers involving diagnostic testing, financing, medicine availability, and continuity of supply; however, these findings are perceptions and reported practices, not representative national or regional estimates or audited health-system data. They identify candidate implementation priorities that require confirmation through patient-level registries and objective access data.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of nafamostat mesilate for anticoagulation during ECMO/CRRT: insight from the integrated meta-analysis and FAERS pharmacovigilance study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) require a balance between maintaining circuit patency and minimizing bleeding risk. Nafamostat mesilate (NM) is a short-acting anticoagulant with distinctive pharmacokinetic properties, including rapid metabolism and a short half-life, which may reduce prolonged systemic anticoagulant exposure. These characteristics make NM a potential alternative to conventional anticoagulation strategies, particularly for patients at high risk of bleeding. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of NM as an anticoagulant for ECMO/CRRT. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang Data were systematically searched for randomized controlled trials and cohort studies comparing NM with sodium citrate, unfractionated heparin (UFH), or no anticoagulation. A meta-analysis was conducted to evaluate filter lifespan, bleeding events, thromboembolic events, and 28-day/intensive care unit (ICU) mortality. Reporting characteristics and potential safety signals for the three anticoagulants were also compared using data from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS). RESULTS: The meta-analysis included 17 studies involving 1,893 patients. Filter lifespan did not differ significantly between the NM and control groups (mean difference [MD] = 1.29 h; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.09-3.66), whereas the risk of bleeding events was significantly lower in the NM group (odds ratio [OR] = 0.61; 95% CI, 0.43-0.86). Subgroup analyses showed that NM was associated with a significantly lower risk of bleeding than sodium citrate (OR = 0.53; 95% CI, 0.31-0.90) and no anticoagulation (OR = 0.41; 95% CI, 0.19-0.90); sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of this finding. The FAERS analysis included 24,238 reports, comprising 233 for NM, 1,612 for sodium citrate, and 22,393 for UFH, with distinct reporting profiles observed among the three anticoagulants. Representative signals for NM included disseminated intravascular coagulation (n = 17; ROR = 112.68, 95% CI: 69.69-182.19), gastrointestinal hemorrhage (n = 12; ROR = 15.44, 95% CI: 8.74-27.29), and decreased platelet count (n = 13; ROR = 7.52, 95% CI: 4.35-13.00). CONCLUSION: NM may reduce bleeding risk while maintaining a filter lifespan comparable to that achieved with other anticoagulation strategies, potentially providing an individualized anticoagulation option for patients at high risk of bleeding. In clinical practice, coagulation abnormalities, changes in platelet counts, and bleeding-related events should be closely monitored.

articles.title: The selective SIK2/3 inhibitor GLPG3970 exhibits antidepressant-like effects via the hippocampal SIK2-CRTC1-CREB-BDNF pathway in chronic stress models.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Depression is a common mental disorder driven by biopsychosocial factors. Although traditional antidepressants serve as first-line therapies, they face clinical challenges, underscoring the need for novel therapeutic agents with improved efficacy. Our previous studies have identified hippocampal SIK2 as a key regulator in the pathogenesis of depression, acting through the cAMP response element-binding protein (CREB)-regulated transcription coactivator 1 (CRTC1)-CREB-brain derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) signaling pathway. In this study, we investigated the antidepressant-like effects of GLPG3970, a novel selective inhibitor of SIK2/3, in male C57BL/6J mice. METHODS: Chronic social defeat stress (CSDS) and chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) models of depression were employed, combined with behavioral tests, virus-mediated gene transfer, Western blotting, co-immunoprecipitation, and immunofluorescence. RESULTS: It was found that repeated administration of GLPG3970 significantly suppressed depressive-like behaviors in both CSDS and CUMS model mice, blocked stress-induced increases in hippocampal SIK2 expression and CRTC1 cytoplasmic translocation, and consequently restored the hippocampal BDNF signaling cascade and neurogenesis. More importantly, by using adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated overexpression of SIK2 or silencing of CRTC1/CREB/BDNF in the hippocampus, the antidepressant-like effects of GLPG3970 in mice were notably eliminated. DISCUSSION: Collectively, these findings together demonstrate that the antidepressant-like actions of GLPG3970 in mice depend on the hippocampal SIK2-CRTC1-CREB-BDNF signaling pathway, highlighting its potential as a novel candidate for antidepressant therapy.

articles.title: PMEPA1 attenuates myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury via interaction with NEDD4 and involvement of the TGF-β/SMAD pathway.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) remains a significant challenge in cardiovascular medicine, and its molecular mechanisms are not yet fully elucidated. METHODS: In the present study, integrated transcriptomic analysis combined with machine learning identified PMEPA1 as a key gene consistently downregulated in both rat models of MIRI and H9c2 cardiomyocytes subjected to ischemia -reperfusion injury. A series of in vivo and in vitro experiments, including gene overexpression and knockdown, cell viability and proliferation assays, flow cytometry, Western blot, co-immunoprecipitation, and immunofluorescence, were performed to investigate the role and underlying mechanism of PMEPA1 in MIRI. RESULTS: Overexpression of PMEPA1 enhanced cardiomyocyte proliferation, reduced apoptosis, and inhibited activation of the TGF-β/SMAD signaling pathway. Further investigation revealed a direct interaction between PMEPA1 and the E3 ubiquitin ligase NEDD4. Both NEDD4 overexpression and PMEPA1 knockdown aggravated cardiomyocyte injury and increased activation of the TGF-β/SMAD pathway. Notably, the detrimental effects of NEDD4 overexpression were attenuated in the absence of PMEPA1, suggesting a PMEPA1-dependent mechanism. DISCUSSION: These findings highlight a novel NEDD4-PMEPA1 axis in the regulation of TGF-β/SMAD signaling during myocardial injury and provide new insights into potential molecular targets for the treatment of cardiovascular disease.

articles.title: Ensemble signal detection reveals target-specific temporal risk of hypokalemia after immune checkpoint inhibition: a translational pharmacology framework.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized cancer treatment, but traditional pharmacovigilance lacks a translational computational framework capable of resolving target-specific nonlinear temporal risks of adverse events such as hypokalemia. METHODS: We integrated 3,243 ICI-related hypokalemia reports from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) and VigiBase (2014-2024). An ensemble signal-detection strategy cross-validated four disproportionality algorithms (Reporting Odds Ratio [ROR], Proportional Reporting Ratio [PRR], Empirical Bayesian Geometric Mean [EBGM], and Information Component [IC]). Flexible nonlinear survival analysis was performed using restricted cubic spline (RCS) Cox regression to model time-to-event dynamics. RESULTS: Programmed Death-Ligand 1 (PD-L1) inhibitors triggered the strongest signal (ROR = 3.20, 95% CI: 2.95-3.48), with ultra-early onset (median 23 days) and the highest case fatality rate (23.7%). An asymmetric biphasic mortality pattern showed a nadir at 60 days: early-onset (≤30 days) hypokalemia peaked at a hazard ratio (HR) of ∼1.9, whereas late-onset (>90 days) risk gradually rose to HR ∼1.8 within 350 days. Programmed Death-1 (PD-1) inhibitors significantly increased severe hypokalemia risk (odds ratio [OR] = 28.32), with male predominance across PD-1 and CTLA-4 subgroups. DISCUSSION: This interpretable ensemble framework reveals target-specific temporal toxicity signatures from multi-source real-world data, providing a computationally grounded translational pharmacology foundation for precision electrolyte monitoring and mechanism-informed safety prediction.

articles.title: Online adaptive E-tutorials for development of critical appraisal skills.
articles.abstract: Critical appraisal of research literature is an important skill for graduates yet science graduate employers report dissatisfaction with skill levels. As scaffolding can assist in critical appraisal development, we aimed to develop and evaluate 2 adaptive e-tutorials for critical appraisal development of neuropharmacology research articles as part of the scaffolding process. We developed adaptive e-tutorials allowing personalised feedback and remediation. Results of an end-of-tutorial survey, and comparisons of institutional Unit of Study Survey ratings and exam results in the 2 years before, and during, the intervention were analysed. Over 4 years, 150 students participated. In the cohorts that did not complete the e-tutorial, there were significant differences in exam marks between students of different academic backgrounds (non-science < science < medicine backgrounds; p < 0.05), while no significant differences between groups were seen in students that completed the e-tutorial, and these marks were statistically equivalent. Students ranked their perceived benefit from the videos, increase in critical appraisal ability, and value of the e-tutorial with average rankings between 4.4-4.6 on a Likert scale (5 = strongly agree). Similarly, students who completed the e-tutorial showed a significant increase in rating of their critical thinking skills in the Unit of Study Survey (p < 0.05). Completion of the e-tutorial was associated with increased equitable development of critical appraisal. Students from non-science backgrounds showed the biggest increase in actual appraisal performance, suggesting that while the e-tutorial was associated with increased confidence for all students, the other features of the course may have developed appraisal levels to a stage sufficient for successful exam completion.

articles.title: Systematic review of clinical trials and cohort studies evaluating HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) regimens to inform updated Canadian guidelines.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: We conducted a systematic review of clinical trials and cohort studies on HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) regimens to inform updated 2025 Canadian guidelines. METHODS: We searched Medline and Embase (July 2017-June 2024) for studies reporting on: HIV acquisition, PEP completion, adverse events (AEs) leading to discontinuation and/or moderate to severe adverse events. Two reviewers independently screened abstracts and publications and extracted data from eligible articles. RESULTS: Of 5226 abstracts screened, we retrieved 112 full-text articles and included 22. Median study size was 160 (range = 52-26 988) participants. Regimens included DTG + TDF/XTC (n = 4, 18%), EVG/c/TDF/FTC (n = 4, 18%), BIC/TAF/FTC (n = 4, 18%), RAL + TDF/FTC (n = 4, 18%), EVG/c/TAF/FTC (n = 3, 14%), RPV/TDF/FTC (n = 2, 9%), DOR/TDF/FTC (n = 2, 9%), MVC + TDF/FTC (n = 1, 5%), a wide variety of protease inhibitor-based regimens (n = 7, 32%) and novel combinations with the injectable fusion inhibitor albuvirtide (n = 1, 5%); a third of studies included three or more regimens (n = 8, 36%). Among studies examining PEP completion rates (n = 12, 55%), cumulative completion rate was 86.6% (7779/8983 PEP episodes) and appeared highest for RAL + TDF/FTC, BIC/FTC/TAF and DOR/TDF/3TC at 96.4%, 96.3% and 95.0%, respectively. PEP tolerability was good, with few discontinuations due to adverse events; where data were available, this was lowest for INSTI-based regimens at 0.5% (pooled across two studies) for RAL + TDF/FTC, 1.0% (1/99) for DTG + TDF/XTC, 1.8% (2/109) for BIC/TAF/FTC and zero with albuvirtide (0/198). HIV seroconversions were rare (n = 5/8134, 0.06%) and often related to premature PEP discontinuation or repeated exposures. CONCLUSIONS: Multiple PEP regimens have been associated with high completion, good tolerability and rare seroconversion, supporting their inclusion in clinical guidelines.

articles.title: Identification of a novel Microbacterium species and biosynthesis of gold nanoparticles: activation of apoptosis and dysregulation of ABCG transporters in gastric adenocarcinoma cells.
articles.abstract: Gastric cancer has high morbidity and mortality rates worldwide, often requiring new therapeutic approaches. Biosynthesis of gold nanoparticles (GNPs) offers a promising treatment due to their unique biological properties and biocompatibility. In this study, we synthesized gold nanoparticles using the cultural supernatant of Microbacterium sp. MAH-37 (MM37-S) and evaluated their anti-gastric cancer activity, focusing on apoptosis induction and regulation of the ABCG transporter pathway. The Microbacterium sp. strain MAH-37 was isolated from pumpkin garden soil, and its morphology was characterized by transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The successful biosynthesis of MM37-S-GNP was confirmed by UV-visible spectroscopy, SAED, DLS, FTIR, XRD, EDX, and FE-TEM analyses. Biological evaluations revealed that MM37-S-GNPs exhibited cytotoxicity of approximately 72% at 200 µg/mL against AGS cells and confirmed by colony formation and Live/Dead assay, whereas normal HFE-145 cells was non-toxic. Furthermore, Hoechst 33,258, propidium iodide, and Mito Tracker revealed nuclear condensation and fragmentation, membrane-compromised cells, and mitochondrial disruption, respectively, indicating cell death via apoptosis. H2DCFDA staining demonstrated a significant increase intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation in AGS cells following MM37-S-GNP. Flow cytometric analysis revealed that treatment induced apoptosis in AGS cells, with 30.4% apoptotic cells observed at 200 µg/mL. Consistently, mRNA and protein expression levels confirmed apoptosis cell death, as evidenced by an increased Bax/Bcl-2 ratio and elevated levels of cleaved caspase-9. Additionally, Western blot analysis revealed that treatment with higher doses of MM37-S-GNPs significantly downregulated the expression of ABCG1 and ABCG2 transporters. MM37-S-GNPs selectivelyeliminated gastric cancer cells through ROS-mediated mitochondrial damage and apoptotic pathways, while effectively regulating ABCG transporter expression, highlighting their potential as a promising nanotherapeutic agent.

articles.title: Combined antibacterial and antibiofilm activity of an Ag-CeO₂/MgAl-LDH nanocomposite-nanoemulsion formulation against multidrug-resistant Enterococcus faecium.
articles.abstract: The increasing prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) Enterococcus faecium has created an urgent need for alternative antimicrobial strategies capable of overcoming conventional antibiotic resistance and inhibiting biofilm formation. In the present study, the antibacterial and antibiofilm activities of an Ag-CeO₂/MgAl-LDH nanocomposite, a sunflower oil-based nanoemulsion, and their combined formulation were evaluated against both a clinical MDR isolate and the reference strain E. faecium MCC 2763. The prepared formulations were characterized using dynamic light scattering (DLS), zeta potential analysis, and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. Antibacterial activity was assessed by minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC), time-kill kinetics, impedance-based growth monitoring, bacterial adherence assays, and biofilm inhibition studies. The combined nanocomposite-nanoemulsion formulation showed greater antibacterial and antibiofilm activity than the individual formulations under the experimental conditions evaluated. Time-kill and biofilm assays indicated improved inhibition of bacterial growth and biofilm formation, while impedance measurements further supported the antibacterial activity of the combined formulation. Although the present findings demonstrate the promising antibacterial potential of the developed formulation, formal synergy analysis, cytotoxicity evaluation, advanced physicochemical characterization, and mechanistic investigations were beyond the scope of this study. These investigations will be essential in future work to further evaluate the therapeutic potential of this formulation. Overall, the developed Ag-CeO₂/MgAl-LDH nanocomposite-nanoemulsion formulation represents a promising antibacterial platform for combating multidrug-resistant Enterococcus faecium and warrants further investigation through comprehensive preclinical evaluation.

articles.title: PVA/chitosan-based hydrogels integrated with tilapia skin-derived collagen and Urtica dioica offers a promising approach for effective burn wound healing via transcriptional modulation of bFgf, Mmp2, Jak/Stat3, and α-Sma signaling pathway.
