articles.abstract: Cutaneous wound repair is governed by a highly coordinated physiological cascade that includes recruitment of inflammatory cells, release of cytokine mediators, deposition of extracellular matrix components, and subsequent remodeling of scar tissue. Nowadays, plant extracts are viewed as an efficient alternative for wound healing. Urtica dioica (U. dioica) is rich in diverse bioactive plant compounds with varied therapeutic effects and appears to support skin wound repair. However, the molecular mechanisms and signaling pathways through which they influence regenerating tissues and cells remain poorly understood. This study aimed to confirm the signaling cascade and mechanism of topical application of a hydrogel formulation incorporated with tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus L.) skin-derived collagen and U. dioica extract on the skin regeneration process based on histopathological, TEM assessment as well as analyze alterations in the expression of key wound healing-related genes, such as Jak/Stat3, Smad3, fibroblast growth factor 2 (fgf2) genes, Acta2 ( α smooth muscle actin), and matrix metalloproteinases (Mmp2) gene in rat burn model. UPLC-ESI-MS/MS also analyzed the chemical composition of U. dioica. Thirty-five animals were randomly allocated to seven groups (n = 5 per group): negative control (NCtrl; no treatment), positive control (PCtrl), hydrogel base treated group (Hgb G), tilapia collagen hydrogel (ColHgb G), MEBO® cream (MEBO G), U. dioica extract (UD G), and a combination of collagen hydrogel plus U. dioica extract (ColHgb-UD G). Burn wound (2 × 2 cm) were made on the back of each generally anaesthetized rat, and wound surface area was measured on days 0, 3, 6, 9, 12, and 15 post-burn. The animals were then sacrificed, and tissues were collected for histological, TEM, and molecular analysis. Our results showed that the methanolic extract of the aerial parts of Urtica dioica was predominantly composed of flavonoids and fatty acids. Analysis in the negative ionization mode enabled the identification of several flavonoids, including apigenin, isorhamnetin, taxifolin, and eriodictyol, detected in both free and glycosylated forms. Wound closure was faster in the ColHgb-UD group than in the control-positive group. Gene expression patterns showed that U. dioica-treated rats, either alone or mixed with collagen hydrogel, notably inhibited the expression of profibrotic factors Jack/Stat3 and Acta2, while activating angiogenesis Fbgf2, Smad3 as well as Mmp2 compared with the positive control group. The histopathological findings showed significant healing progress in the ColHgb-UD group compared with the positive control untreated group and the other treated groups. Results demonstrate superior wound healing performance for ColHgb-UD compared to the control positive group the synergistic effect of U. dioica and collagen showed less scarring, more blood capillaries, less inflammatory cells therefore remarkably healed faster making the extract ideal for wound healing applications and a novel drug candidate for wound healing.

articles.title: The dual role of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR axis in glial cell survival and neuroinflammation.
articles.abstract: Multiple sclerosis is characterized by a triad of inflammation, demyelination, and neurodegeneration, yet current disease-modifying therapies are limited in their ability to halt progressive neurodegeneration or promote remyelination. The PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway is a master regulator of these divergent cellular processes and therefore represents a biological paradox in multiple sclerosis. In the pathogenic facet of the disease, activation of this axis supports the differentiation and effector functions of pro-inflammatory T- and B-cells and contributes to inflammatory programs in microglia and macrophages. In the regenerative facet, physiological PI3K/AKT/mTOR activity is required for oligodendrocyte precursor-cell survival, differentiation, myelin synthesis, and maintenance of myelin integrity. Astrocytic signaling adds another layer of context-dependence, with pathway activity influencing reactive gliosis and the inflammatory or reparative properties of the lesion environment. Consequently, systemic inhibition of the pathway may suppress neuroinflammation while simultaneously interfering with endogenous repair. This review therefore considers PI3K/AKT/mTOR axis according to these opposing pathogenic and protective functions, highlighting the importance of cell type, disease stage, and treatment timing. Precision strategies capable of selectively suppressing inflammatory signaling while preserving or restoring pro-regenerative activity, potentially through cell-specific molecular targets, may provide a more rational therapeutic approach than generalized pathway inhibition.

articles.title: Delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol ameliorates oxidative stress, mitochondrial redox state, and neuroinflammation induced by high-fructose diet.
articles.abstract: This study investigates the effects of a high-fructose diet (HFD) on brain oxidative stress, mitochondrial redox state, and pro-inflammatory cytokine expression, and specifically evaluates whether delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) attenuates these HFD-induced changes. Thirty-two Sprague-Dawley rats were divided into four groups: Control, HFD (10% fructose in drinking water for 12 weeks), THC (1.5 mg/kg daily for the last 4 weeks), and HFD + THC (HFD for 12 weeks with THC co-administration during the final 4 weeks). Biochemical biomarkers (AOPP, DT, KYN, MDA, AGE, T-SH, NADH, FAD, serotonin, insulin) and mRNA expression levels of inflammation-related genes (IL-6, IL-1β, TNF-α, NF-κB) were analyzed in brain tissues. The HFD significantly increased levels of protein oxidation (AOPP, DT, KYN, AGE); lipid peroxidation (MDA); and NADH and FAD fluorescence whilst decreasing total thiol (T-SH) content. HFD also increased the mRNA expression of all inflammatory markers examined. In contrast, THC treatment significantly reduced oxidative damage and NADH and FAD fluorescence and reduced the relative mRNA expression of the investigated inflammation-related genes. Strong positive correlations were observed between pro-inflammatory cytokine mRNA expression and oxidative stress markers. HFD causes significant biochemical and molecular damage to the brain. THC administration was associated with a significant attenuation of HFD-induced oxidative stress, mitochondrial redox state, and pro-inflammatory cytokine expression, suggesting that it may mitigate diet-associated neurochemical perturbations.

articles.title: Comparative hepatoprotective effects of Ginkgo biloba extract and N-Acetylcysteine against methotrexate-induced liver injury in rats: modulation of IκB-α, p38 MAPK, and p53 phosphorylation.
articles.abstract: Methotrexate (MTX) is an effective chemotherapeutic agent whose use can be limited by hepatotoxicity. This study comparatively evaluated the effects of Ginkgo biloba extract (GbE) and N-acetylcysteine (NAC) on MTX-induced liver injury, focusing on oxidative stress, inflammatory and apoptotic responses, and associated hepatic phosphorylation of Inhibitor of nuclear factor kappa-B alpha (IκB-α), p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (p38 MAPK), and tumor protein p53 (p53), key components of stress-responsive signaling pathways. Thirty-two adult male rats were randomly assigned to four groups (n = 8/group). MTX (20 mg/kg, i.p.) was administered once on Day 4. GbE or NAC (200 mg/kg, p.o.) was administered for 3 days before and 6 days after MTX exposure. Serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT), total and direct bilirubin and hepatic malondialdehyde (MDA), nitric oxide (NO), reduced glutathione (GSH), catalase (CAT), superoxide dismutase (SOD), tumor necrosis factor- alpha (TNF-α), interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β), Bcl-2-associated X protein (Bax), and B-cell lymphoma 2 (Bcl-2) were assessed. Hepatic phosphorylation of IκBα, p38 MAPK, and p53 was evaluated by Western blotting. MTX significantly (P < 0.001) increased serum ALT by 120% and hepatic MDA, TNF-α, IL-1β and Bax by 127%, 386%, 163%, and 439%, respectively, while reducing GSH and Bcl-2 by 66% and 63%, relative to control. Phosphorylation of IκBα, p38 MAPK, and p53 increased by 35%, 64%, and 68%, respectively. GbE and NAC significantly (P < 0.001) attenuated these alterations, with NAC producing generally greater effects than GbE. GbE and NAC attenuated MTX-induced hepatic injury across interconnected oxidative, inflammatory, apoptotic, and signaling endpoints. NAC showed a generally stronger response under the conditions tested. These findings support further investigation of both agents as potential strategies for mitigating MTX-associated hepatotoxicity.

articles.title: Chemogenetic inhibition of the ventrolateral orbitofrontal cortex disrupts novelty-guided updating of spatial memories and alters hippocampal engram reactivation.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Adaptive behavior requires revising memories when outcomes deviate from expectations. The orbitofrontal cortex (OFC) is implicated in representing outcome expectancies, but its role in memory-updating, beyond value-based learning, remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: We tested whether the ventrolateral OFC (VLO) contributes to hippocampal-dependent memory-updating in the Objects in Updated Locations (OUL) task, where novelty-driven exploration provides a behavioral readout consistent with successful updating of spatial information. METHODS: Using inhibitory DREADDs, in male and female (Swiss Webster and C57BL/6) mice, we suppressed VLO activity during the Updating session, when new object-location information was introduced. RESULTS: Control mice preferentially explored the updated object-location configuration during Updating and discriminated between updated and novel object-location configurations at Test, whereas VLO-inhibited mice did not. VLO inhibition when no updating demand was present did not alter exploration of novel object-location configurations or memory for the original spatial configuration at Test. CONCLUSIONS: These results indicate that VLO activity is selectively required when novelty must be interpreted relative to prior experience, implicating this region in evaluating change rather than detecting it. To assess hippocampal ensemble dynamics, we tagged neuronal ensembles, in the dorsal dentate gyrus (dDG) recruited during Updating, followed by quantification of overlap between Updating-tagged cells and ensembles reactivated at Test. We found that VLO inhibition reduced reactivation of Updating-tagged dDG ensembles, paralleling the behavioral impairments observed in the OUL task. These findings support a role for the VLO in hippocampal-dependent memory-updating and extend OFC models beyond reward contexts to include predictive updating of spatial memory representations. CLINICAL TRIAL: Not applicable.

articles.title: Beyond Nanosizing: Mechanism-Guided Design and Rational Selection of Polymeric and Lipid Nanocarriers for Translatable Drug Delivery.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nanosizing can modify dissolution and carrier behaviour, but particle size alone does not determine clinically useful exposure. OBJECTIVE: To compare polymeric and lipid-based nanocarriers using a mechanism-guided framework that links payload properties, composition, process conditions, biological barriers, critical quality attributes (CQAs), and translational risk. METHODS: A critical narrative review with a structured scoping update was performed using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar during manuscript preparation. The intended publication window was 2010-2025, with earlier seminal studies retained where mechanistically necessary. Because exact search dates, an auditable database export, screening counts, and independent-reviewer records were not preserved, this review is not presented as a systematic review and no pooled effect estimate is reported. RESULTS: Polymeric systems can stabilize selected amorphous or molecularly dispersed payloads and tune release through diffusion, hydration, and degradation, whereas lipid systems can support lipid-phase solubilization, digestion-dependent oral absorption, membrane interaction, and nucleic-acid delivery. Across both classes, precipitation, release failure, phase transformation, protein-corona and immune effects, endosomal sequestration, and process drift can disconnect favorable in vitro attributes from human pharmacology. Clinical examples show product-specific changes in disposition, safety, or efficacy rather than a universal bioavailability multiplier. CONCLUSION: Rational nanocarrier selection should start from a testable mechanism and a defined translational risk, then be challenged with route-relevant biological assays, exposure measurements, safety data, and manufacturing comparability. The proposed framework is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation.

articles.title: Early disease control with a biochemical response to aumolertinib after postoperative recurrence of EGFR-Mutant stage IIIA lung adenocarcinoma after icotinib, with EGFR T790M detected at recurrence: a Case Report.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) are a standard treatment for EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, acquired resistance commonly develops after treatment with first- or second-generation EGFR-TKIs. Aumolertinib, a third-generation EGFR-TKI, has demonstrated efficacy in tumors harboring the EGFR exon 20 T790M resistance mutation. CASE PRESENTATION: A 57-year-old man with stage IIIA lung adenocarcinoma and a history of hypertension and long-term smoking underwent thoracoscopic lobectomy with intrapulmonary lymph node dissection. Postoperative molecular testing identified an EGFR exon 19 deletion, and adjuvant oral icotinib (375 mg/d) was initiated. After treatment discontinuation, disease recurrence was detected on PET-CT involving the right hilar lymph nodes and a right pleural/subpleural lesion, which was confirmed by biopsy. Repeat molecular testing revealed concurrent EGFR exon 19 deletion and EGFR exon 20 T790M mutation. After 1 month of aumolertinib treatment, the target lesion decreased in size from 24 to 23 mm and was assessed as stable disease according to RECIST version 1.1, whereas the serum CEA level decreased from 24.19 to 4.35 ng/mL, indicating early disease control with a biochemical response. CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates early disease control and a biochemical response to aumolertinib treatment in recurrent NSCLC with an EGFR exon 20 T790M mutation detected at recurrence. It also highlights the importance of repeat molecular testing to guide therapeutic decisions.

articles.title: Snail-shRNA in AAV9 inhibited EMT and pulmonary fibrosis in silica-instilled mice.
articles.abstract: Our previous study in vitro has shown that targeting transcription factor Snail might be a strategy for the treatment of silicosis. In this study, we evaluated the feasibility of the strategy in vivo. Here we used CBG transgenic mice which could be used to track and isolate alveolar epithelial type II cells (AT II cells) to confirm that 2.5mg silica could induce epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in AT II cells in vivo. Based on the results that 2.5mg silica induced a rapid elevation of Snail in the lungs of mice and the optimal injection dose and stable expression time of adeno-associated virus (AAV) 9 vectors, we finally decided to inject AAV9-mediated Snail knockdown at 1.0×1011 vg/mouse 1 week before silica instillation to inhibit the levels of Snail increased by silica. The results showed that Snail-shRNA in AAV9 prevented silica-induced EMT in AT II cells in CBG transgenic mice and inhibited EMT and pulmonary fibrosis induced by silica in wild-type mice. Quantitative proteomic analysis combined with dbEMT database mapping further indicated that Snail knockdown suppressed silica-induced EMT and fibrosis through a Fibronectin (FN1)-centered interaction network involving proMMP8 activation and JUN kinase signaling. These findings suggested that Snail could be used as a target for the treatment of pulmonary fibrosis in the future.

articles.title: An electrospun PCL/PVA-chitosan nanofiber scaffold loaded with selenium nanoparticles promotes antibacterial activity and accelerates wound healing: synthesis, characterization, and in-vivo evaluation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic, epidermal full-thickness wounds present a critical clinical challenge due to high risks of infection, impaired healing, and lack of advanced dressings that synergistically combine antibacterial efficacy with tissue regeneration. OBJECTIVE: This study aims to design and evaluate a multifunctional nanofibrous scaffold that simultaneously addresses anti-infection, mechanical support, and controlled tissue remodeling. METHODS: A tri-component nanofibrous scaffold composed of polyvinyl alcohol, chitosan, and polycaprolactone was fabricated via electrospinning. Selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) were incorporated to impart antibacterial and pro-healing properties. The scaffold was characterized for morphological, mechanical, and biological attributes. In vivo performance was assessed using a murine epidermal full-thickness wound model. RESULTS: The scaffold demonstrated significantly enhanced mechanical properties and exhibited potent antibacterial activity against S. aureus and E. coli. Controlled release of SeNPs reduced initial cytotoxic burst effects. In vivo tests confirmed accelerated wound closure and superior tissue regeneration compared to controls CONCLUSION: The SeNP-functionalized nanofibrous scaffold represents a promising therapeutic platform for epidermal full-thickness wound healing, effectively combining mechanical robustness, antibacterial action, and biocompatibility.

articles.title: Vilazodone Hydrochloride-Loaded Nanostructured Lipid Carrier In Situ Gel for Intranasal Nose-to-Brain Antidepressant Delivery.
articles.abstract: The Oral delivery of vilazodone hydrochloride (VLZ), a serotonin partial agonist-reuptake inhibitor for major depressive disorder, suffers from extensive hepatic first-pass metabolism, food-dependent absorption, and poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, limiting its central therapeutic impact. Here, VLZ-loaded nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs) were engineered and embedded within a Poloxamer 407/188-chitosan thermosensitive in situ gel to enable direct nose-to-brain delivery. The NLCs were fabricated by combined high-shear and high-pressure homogenisation and optimised through central composite design, yielding a batch with particle size 24.74 ± 2.23 nm, polydispersity index 0.248 ± 0.012, and entrapment efficiency 91.37 ± 4.56%. The lyophilised NLCs were incorporated into an in situ gel with a physiologically appropriate gelation temperature of 34°C and gelation time of 42 s. Fourier Transform Infrared FTIR spectroscopy confirmed complete drug encapsulation, evidenced by disappearance of the diagnostic nitrile (C≡N) absorption band, while DSC and XRPD verified conversion of VLZ to an amorphous state within the lipid matrix. Drug release followed Korsmeyer-Peppas kinetics, sustained over 24 h, and the formulation remained stable under refrigerated storage. In Swiss albino mice, the intranasal NLC-in situ gel (1 mg/kg) produced a profound antidepressant-like effect relative to oral pure drug (10 mg/kg) across open field, tail suspension, and sucrose preference tests, consistent with enhanced nose-to-brain delivery via the olfactory and trigeminal pathways. Hence this nanocarrier-hydrogel strategy offers a promising, non-invasive route to enhanced CNS delivery of antidepressants.
